exercise.name: Leg Press Calf Raise
library_steps: Sit in the leg press, toes on the bottom edge of the plate.
Push the plate up and keep your legs almost straight.
Point your toes to push the plate further, then let it come back slowly.
Use a weight you control so your feet never slip off the edge.
exercise.one_line_summary: Reclined in the leg press, legs nearly straight, balls of the feet on the lower edge of the plate. Picture 1: heels dropped below the toes (calves stretched); picture 2: ankles pushed out, plate pressed away on the toes. Knees stay the same.

setup.target: Balls of the feet on the plate edge, heels off; feet hip-width, toes forward.

muscles.emg: Knee-straight calf-raise training grows the gastrocnemius more than seated raises (S1); both heads highly active in heel raises (S2).

muscles.role: Hold the knees almost straight against the plate.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Knees bend to push the plate.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Turns it into a leg press; keep knees still (S1).

sources.citation: Kinoshita M, Maeo S, Kobayashi Y, et al. Triceps surae muscle hypertrophy is greater after standing versus seated calf-raise training. Front Physiol. 2023;14:1272106.
sources.what_it_gave: Training with the knee extended (standing) grew the gastrocnemius far more than knee-bent (seated) calf raises; the knee-straight position loads the gastrocnemius.

sources.citation: Riemann BL, Limbaugh GK, Eitner JD, LeFavi RG. Medial and lateral gastrocnemius activation differences during heel-raise exercise with three different foot positions. J Strength Cond Res. 2011;25(3):634-639.
sources.what_it_gave: Heel raises with feet neutral, in and out: both gastrocnemius heads highly active; foot angle shifts the medial/lateral split.

clip_check.target: ~17 deg dorsiflexed -> ~27 deg plantarflexed (start -25 to -10, end 20-40)

clip_check.check: Machine parts meet the hands/feet; levers keep their length
clip_check.target: moving rod lengths equal at start and end (+-1 cm)
